topics.title: Appendix A — The Systems Programmer’s Diagnostic Desk Reference
topics.summary: A useful diagnostic starts with the narrowest claim the evidence can support. “The descriptor is valid” is weaker than “the descriptor identifies the intended open resource.” “The thread returned” is weaker than “every accepted task completed.” “The payload parsed” is weaker than “the peer was authenticated.” This reference organizes recurring failures by the boundary that needs investigation, not by the last function name visible in a stack trace.

topics.title: Preserve the first useful evidence
topics.summary: Record the operation, the relevant owned object, the exact return channel, the progress already made, and the intended next state. Capture errno immediately for interfaces that use it. Preserve direct error values for interfaces such as posix_spawn and getaddrinfo that do not follow the same convention. Do not overwrite the original cause with an unrelated cleanup error; report both when the completion policy requires it.

blocks.text: A diagnostic record should be bounded. Include numeric endpoints, resource roles, phase names, and counts rather than copying unlimited input or secret-bearing buffers. An attacker-controlled payload is not a safe log template. The teaching service uses category counters and does not log request contents. A production logging adapter would need its own retention, privacy, and failure behavior.

topics.title: A resource incident, worked through
topics.summary: Suppose a service’s descriptor count rises during rejected requests. Begin with a reproducible owned fixture, not by changing the process limit. Trace a connection from accept to queue admission. If admission rejects, determine whether the argument was consumed by value, returned to the caller, or leaked through an unowned integer. An ownership wrapper should close the rejected connection when its local value leaves scope.

blocks.text: A resource incident, worked through

Suppose a service’s descriptor count rises during rejected requests. Begin with a reproducible owned fixture, not by changing the process limit. Trace a connection from accept to queue admission. If admission rejects, determine whether the argument was consumed by value, returned to the caller, or leaked through an unowned integer. An ownership wrapper should close the rejected connection when its local value leaves scope.

An ownership wrapper should close the rejected connection when its local value leaves scope.

blocks.text: Next examine the successful path. The worker receives one owner, processes one request, and destroys that owner after completion or failure. A reference to the native descriptor is only a borrow for a call. It must not be copied into a delayed task after the worker’s owner is destroyed. Distinguish a leak from a stale-descriptor bug: the latter can close or use an unrelated resource after the number is reused.

blocks.text: Use a bounded repeated test and inspect resource state before and after quiescence. A changing count while work is in flight can be legitimate. Compare at a point where all relevant workers have joined and all temporary owners have been destroyed. The same principle applies to allocations, mappings, and child processes: the observation boundary must match the lifecycle claim.

topics.title: A stalled request, worked through
topics.summary: A worker waits for the rest of a frame. Identify whether it is reading the header or the body, how many bytes were accepted, the maximum allowed length, and the absolute deadline. If a per-call timeout is recreated on each read, a slowly progressing client can renew it indefinitely. The extended adapter carries the same deadline through the complete request and response operation.

blocks.text: A readiness event does not guarantee that the next nonblocking read completes the requested transfer. Retry temporary unavailability through the readiness loop while preserving progress and deadline. Interpret EOF according to the frame state. An error after a response prefix was sent leaves an externally visible partial effect; it is not a clean rollback to “nothing happened.”

blocks.text: When stop is requested, verify that every blocked operation can observe it. The extended server polls in short bounded slices and checks stop state rather than assuming a cross-thread close safely cancels another thread’s descriptor use. This is a cooperative design on an ordinary scheduler. A twenty-five-millisecond poll slice is not a promise of twenty-five-millisecond worst-case shutdown under all scheduling conditions.

topics.title: A race investigation, worked through
topics.summary: Identify the conflicting accesses, the object whose lifetime contains them, and the synchronization relationship intended to order them. Do not stop at a line saying atomic or mutex. A mutex protects accesses only when all participating paths obey the same discipline. A release operation publishes data only through the corresponding observation relationship, and reuse requires its own handoff.

blocks.text: Run a race detector where the environment supports it, but preserve the source-level argument even when the tool reports no issue. Instrumentation observes executions; it does not enumerate all allowed schedules. Conversely, an unavailable race-detector runtime must be reported as unavailable, not converted into a clean test result. The package’s verification report distinguishes successful compiler/sanitizer runs from any unsupported diagnostic attempt.

topics.title: The recovery question
topics.summary: For every incident, ask what changed outside the current process. Memory cleanup can release local owners; it cannot retract bytes already delivered, reverse a child program’s completed file mutation, or guarantee that a remote request was never executed. Recovery needs an application protocol when external effects are involved. Local exception safety and distributed outcome certainty are different guarantees.

blocks.text: Close the investigation with a bounded regression case and a statement of the corrected invariant. “Added a sleep” is not a synchronization explanation. “Raised the buffer size” is not a framing explanation. “Retried every error” is not an ownership explanation. A repair is defensible when its mechanism addresses the specific failed boundary and its tests would distinguish that repair from the original misleading success.
